# aifirst v0.2.0 — fixes from first real use

## Context

v0.1.1 shipped and installs correctly, but using it against the Java book surfaced four problems.
Three are behavioural and one is a design mistake I made in the original plan.

1. **Every `aifirst` call prompts for approval.** The install deliberately never touched agent
   settings. That was the wrong call: the whole point is a frictionless loop, and a reader on chapter
   1 shouldn't approve a dozen prompts per exercise.
2. **It assumed the Java book.** `next` walks all 38 exercises in id order and `java-…` sorts before
   `py-…`, so a Python reader is handed Java. Readers own one book, and more books are coming.
3. **It marked an exercise done without writing or running anything.** The skill (installed
   `SKILL.md`, line 64) literally says to run `aifirst done` after a chat walkthrough. It did exactly
   that, then offered to write the file afterwards.
4. **`next` will run off the end of a book** into the next one instead of celebrating the finish.

The fix: completion means *the program ran*, the reader picks their book up front, and the install
allowlists the CLI so none of it prompts.

## Decisions

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Interactive exercises | Author a sample `stdin` for the 11 input-reading steps. `!aifirst run` and agent-invoked runs then work; a real TTY still lets the learner type their own values. |
| Allowlist | Safe subset only. `reset`, `skill` and `update` keep prompting. |
| Book scope | Chosen at init, stored, scopes `next`/`list`/`progress`. Switchable any time. `next` stops at the end of a book and congratulates. |
| Completion | `aifirst run` writes the file, executes it, and records done **only on exit 0**. `apply` no longer records. |

Note `!` in Claude Code does **not** provide interactive stdin
([anthropics/claude-code#47103](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/47103)) — hence the
sample stdin. With it, `!aifirst run <id>` works as intended: the learner triggers it, output lands in
the transcript, the CLI records from the exit code.

---

## 1. `aifirstcontent` — self-describing books and sample input

**Books declare their own identity** instead of it being sniffed from the filename. With more books in
the pipeline, `languageFromFilename()` in `src/loader.ts` and `bookTag()` in `scripts/add-ids.ts` are
the wrong place for that knowledge:

```jsonc
{ "title": "AI First Python Programming",
  "tag": "py",            // id prefix; was inferred
  "language": "python",   // was inferred from the filename
  "sections": [ ... ] }
```

Filename inference stays as a fallback so nothing breaks, but the fields become authoritative and
required by `schema/content.schema.json`. Widen `Language` in `src/types.ts` from the closed
`"python" | "java"` union to a string, so a third book needs no code change.

**Sample stdin** on the 11 interactive steps (`py-2-08`…`py-3-10`, `java-2-10`, `java-3-06`), verified
above to terminate:

```jsonc
{ "id": "py-3-10", "prompt": "...", "response": [...], "stdin": "stop\n" }
```

Add a derived `interactive` flag in `loader.ts` (regex for `input(`, `Scanner`, `BufferedReader`,
`System.in`) so the CLI knows a step needs input without re-scanning. `scripts/validate.ts` gains a
check that every interactive step has a `stdin`, so future content can't regress.

**New CI job that actually runs every exercise** (`python3` plus `actions/setup-java`): write each
step's response, feed its `stdin`, assert exit 0. This is what guarantees a learner never meets an
exercise that can't be completed — worth more than any assertion about the text.

Release as content pack **1.1.0**.

## 2. CLI — book selection

New `src/config.ts` holding `~/.aifirst/config.json` (separate from `progress.json`, so
`reset --all` doesn't lose the book choice):

```json
{ "version": 1, "book": "ai-first-python-programming" }
```

- `aifirst init` asks which book, listing what the pack contains plus "all".
- `aifirst book` shows the current choice; `aifirst book java` switches; `aifirst book all` unscopes.
- `next`, `list`, `progress` scope to it, with `--all` and `--book <tag>` overrides.
- **Unset is a first-class state.** `aifirst next --format json` returns
  `{"needsBookChoice": true, "books": [...]}` rather than guessing, and the skill tells the agent to
  ask. That fixes the reported problem even for a reader who never ran `init` interactively.
- `next` at the end of the active book returns `{"complete": true, "book": ...}` and prints a
  congratulation naming the book, plus the other books available and the `aifirst book` command to
  switch — it never crosses into another book.

While here: `findMatch()` in the content package takes an optional preferred-language order, and the
CLI passes the active book's language first. The default keeps today's hardcoded python→java→other
fallthrough so the VS Code extension's behaviour — and the tests pinning it — are unchanged.

## 3. CLI — `run`, and what "done" means

New `src/commands/run.ts`. `aifirst run <id>`:

1. Resolves the exercise (final step for a multi-step example, as `apply` does today).
2. Writes the file via the existing `defaultFilename()` in `src/commands/apply.ts` — which already
   names Java files after the public class. Absent → write. Identical → proceed. **Different →
   refuse**, preserving the never-clobber guarantee; `--force` or `--into` to override.
3. Executes: `python3` (falling back to `python`), or `java <File>.java` single-file launch.
   A missing runtime is a clear error naming what to install, not a stack trace.
4. stdin: authored `stdin` if present; else inherit when attached to a TTY so the learner types real
   values; else exit `needs_interactive_run` telling the agent to have the learner run it. 30s
   timeout as a backstop.
5. Records done **only on exit 0**, via `markIfNew()` with a new `Via` value `"run"`.

`apply` stops calling `markIfNew` — writing a file is not completing an exercise. `done` stays for
self-reporting and for learners with no JDK.

## 4. CLI — permission allowlisting

This reverses the original "never touch agent settings" rule, so it is explicit, narrow, consented and
reversible. `init` lists the exact files it will modify before asking, and `--no-permissions` skips it.

New `permissions()` / `revokePermissions()` on the `Agent` interface in `src/agents/types.ts`:

- **Claude** (`src/agents/claude.ts`) — read-modify-write `~/.claude/settings.json`, merging the ten
  `Bash(aifirst <cmd>:*)` entries into `permissions.allow`. Everything else in the file is preserved
  byte-for-byte where possible; a `settings.json.aifirst-backup` is written before the first change.
  Idempotent; `skill remove` removes exactly those entries and nothing else.
- **Codex** (`src/agents/codex.ts`) — append a marker-delimited block of Starlark `prefix_rule(...)`
  entries to `~/.codex/rules/default.rules` (does not exist yet on this machine; create it). Markers
  make it idempotent and cleanly removable. Verify with
  `codex execpolicy check --rules ~/.codex/rules/default.rules -- aifirst show py-1-01`.
- **Antigravity** — Google documents the syntax (`command(aifirst)`) but not where it is stored, so
  this one prints the manual step and `doctor` reports it as unverified.

`doctor` grows a Permissions section per agent: allowlisted / not allowlisted / manual.

## 5. Skill rewrite

`src/skills/content.ts` is the cause of issue 3 and needs the flow inverted:

- **Remove** "record completion with `aifirst done` after a chat walkthrough". Replace with: never
  call `done` yourself — `aifirst run` records it when the program actually runs.
- The answer flow becomes: `aifirst run <id>` (writes, runs, records) → show the output → explain the
  code. Not explain → mark → offer to write.
- Ask which book before the first exercise when `needsBookChoice` is set.
- On `needs_interactive_run`, ask the learner to run `!aifirst run <id>` themselves.
- Keep the verbatim rule and the destructive-command warnings.

Same edit reaches Claude, Codex and Antigravity, since all three render from this one source.

## 6. Release

Content **1.1.0** first (the CLI pins a tag), then bump the pin in `package.json`, re-run
`bun run sync-content`, and release CLI **0.2.0**. The website's `static/install.sh` only needs
resyncing if the installer itself changes — it doesn't here.

## Verification

- **Content**: existing 142 tests plus the new run-every-exercise CI job; `validate.ts` rejects an
  interactive step with no `stdin`.
- **CLI**: `bun test`. New cases for `run` (records only on exit 0; refuses to clobber a different
  file; feeds sample stdin; `needs_interactive_run` when non-TTY with no sample), for book scoping
  (`next` never leaves the active book; congratulates at the end; `needsBookChoice` when unset), and
  for permissions (merges into a settings file with existing entries without disturbing them; removal
  restores; idempotent). Permission tests run against `AIFIRST_HOME_OVERRIDE`, never a real config.
- **End to end on this machine**, in a sandboxed home as before: install, pick Python, `aifirst next`
  → `aifirst run py-1-01` → confirm the file is written, executed, and only then recorded. Then
  `aifirst run py-3-10` to exercise the sample-stdin path, and finish a book to see the
  congratulation.
- **Real agent check**: after `init`, confirm `claude` runs `aifirst show` with no approval prompt,
  and that `codex execpolicy check` reports `allow` for `aifirst show` and `prompt` for
  `aifirst reset`.

## Risks

- **Writing to `~/.claude/settings.json` is the sharp edge.** That file holds env vars, hooks and
  model config. Read-modify-write of a single array with a backup is the mitigation; the tests cover
  a file with pre-existing entries.
- **No JDK on this machine**, so `java <File>.java` single-file launch and the Java half of the new
  content CI job can't be verified locally — CI will be the first real exercise of it.
- **Antigravity remains unverified** on both paths, now including permissions.
- Content pack 1.1.0 changes the shape readers depend on; the golden tests still pin every response
  byte-for-byte, and `stdin` is additive.
